comparison_markdown:
# Slack vs Element

## Overview
Slack and Element are two popular communication platforms designed for teams and organizations. Both tools offer features such as messaging, file sharing, and integrations with other apps. This comparison is beneficial for teams and businesses looking to choose a communication platform that suits their needs.

## Key Differences
* Cost: Slack offers a free plan with limited features, while Element is free and open-source with optional paid support.
* Data ownership: Element allows users to self-host and have full control over their data, whereas Slack stores data on its servers.
* Setup complexity: Slack is generally easier to set up, while Element requires more technical expertise for self-hosting.
* Scalability: Both platforms can scale to meet the needs of large organizations, but Element's self-hosting option provides more flexibility.
* Ecosystem: Slack has a larger ecosystem of integrations with third-party apps, while Element has a growing ecosystem of Matrix-compatible apps.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Slack | Element |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $7.25–$15/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | $362.50–$750/month | $0 (self-hosted) |

## Pros and Cons
### Slack
* Pros:
  + Easy to set up and use
  + Large ecosystem of integrations
  + Good customer support
* Cons:
  + Limited control over data
  + Can be expensive for large teams
  + Limited customization options
### Element
* Pros:
  + Self-hosting option for full data control
  + Free and open-source
  + High customization options
* Cons:
  + Requires technical expertise for self-hosting
  + Smaller ecosystem of integrations
  + Limited customer support

## When to Choose Each
### Slack
Slack is ideal for teams and businesses that prioritize ease of use and a large ecosystem of integrations. It's a good choice for organizations that don't require full control over their data and are willing to pay for a proprietary solution.

### Element
Element is suitable for teams and organizations that value data ownership and customization. It's a good choice for businesses that require a high level of control over their communication platform and are willing to invest time and resources into self-hosting and customization.

## Migration Path
To migrate from Slack to Element, follow these steps:
1. Export your Slack data using Slack's data export tool.
2. Set up an Element server and configure it to your needs.
3. Import your Slack data into Element using the Matrix protocol and Element's import tools.

---
*Data sourced May 2026. Verify current pricing at https://slack.com and https://element.io.*
